clue.text: Arrives for the exam supremely confident, as it happens

definitions.text: Arrives for the exam supremely confident
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone turns up at the test certain of getting through it
an event that occurs or is realised, as a prophecy finally does

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase into 'comes' (arrives) and 'to pass' (aiming to succeed in the exam); 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an event taking place or being fulfilled is exactly this phrase, a set biblical expression.

clue.text: Sign for Mediterranean island cash crop

parts.note: Capri is the island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal grown for sale

explanation.surface: A farmer asks which sign suits a Mediterranean island's money-making harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goat is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, covering late December to January.

clue.text: Ship the troops on it

parts.note: soldiers who serve aboard a vessel are sea-going infantry, so the clue describes them as the troops you put on a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Sea soldiers carried on naval vessels form this corps, such as the Royal or US corps of that name.

clue.text: One feeling guilty? Quite the reverse!…

definitions.text: One feeling guilty? Quite the reverse!…

parts.words: One feeling guilty? Quite the reverse!…
parts.note: turn the idea round: not a person who feels guilty, but a feeling that one is guilty, held by someone else

explanation.definitionFit: Distrust is the feeling that someone is guilty of something, the reverse of personally feeling guilt.

clue.text: And leaves out one — most stupid

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement is a muddled one, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone skips a member of the group, branding them the dimmest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' looks like a description, but it scrambles I and MOST; 'And' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to fail to include it, a straight synonym in the third-person verb form.

clue.text: Stirring call to the industrial troublemaker!

definitions.text: Stirring call to the industrial troublemaker!

parts.words: Stirring call to the industrial troublemaker!
parts.note: the word a shop-floor militant would shout to rouse workers, the verb from which the troublemaker's title comes

explanation.definitionFit: To stir up unrest is to campaign and protest, the activity that gives the factory agitator his name.

clue.text: Try to get elected supporter

definitions.meaning: to run as a candidate in an election, as a British politician does for a seat
a frame or rack that holds something up, such as one for music or umbrellas

explanation.definitionFit: Running for office is what a British candidate does for Parliament, and a rack holding things upright has the same name.

clue.text: Look here! What in the world's going on?

definitions.text: Look here! What in the world's going on?

parts.words: Look here! What in the world's going on?
parts.note: the exasperated exclamation is reread as an invitation to look in the daily news sheet for world events

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is where you look to find out what is happening around the world.

clue.text: Dips into police files when caught

definitions.text: Dips into police files when caught

parts.words: Dips into police files when caught
parts.note: dips is slang for thieves who lift wallets, and such thieves end up in police records once arrested

explanation.definitionFit: Dip is old slang for a thief who steals from people's pockets in crowds.

clue.text: Bent over backwards to help the Crusaders' enemies

definitions.text: Bent over backwards to help the Crusaders' enemies

parts.words: Bent over backwards to help the Crusaders' enemies
parts.note: the idiom about trying hard is reread as curved blades that served the Saracens against the Crusaders

explanation.definitionFit: Curved oriental swords were the typical weapons of the Saracen armies who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: Our lighter planets comprise it

parts.note: our lighter is the sun that lights us, and together with the planets it makes up the whole family around it

explanation.definitionFit: The sun and the bodies orbiting it, Earth included, make up this system.

clue.text: Awkwardly inch it along, initially, for a drink

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means clumsily, so these letters are jumbled
initially means only the opening letter of the word along is used

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles clumsily forward, a little at a time, to fetch a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' scrambles INCH, IT and A (the first letter of 'along', from 'initially'); 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from Tuscany, so an example of a drink.

clue.text: Public outrage directed at the wrong people!

definitions.text: Public outrage directed at the wrong people!

parts.words: Public outrage directed at the wrong people!
parts.note: a disgraceful affair stirs public anger, and the clue hints at the word slander, false charges against innocent people

explanation.definitionFit: A disgrace that shocks people and causes general indignation is this kind of affair.

clue.text: Here draws important vessel back

indicators.note: back means the ship's name is read from end to start

parts.note: a sloop is a small single-masted sailing ship

explanation.surface: An important ship is being drawn backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: On British football pools coupons, betting on match results, score draws are what win, so this is where draws are important.
explanation.definitionFit: The football pools are a British betting game on results where predicting drawn matches is the key to winning.

clue.text: Police officer just below a sergeant

definitions.text: Police officer just below a sergeant

parts.words: Police officer just below a sergeant
parts.note: a British police rank sitting next to sergeant in the ladder of ranks

explanation.walkthrough: In the British police this rank is in fact the one immediately above sergeant; the clue as printed puts it below.
explanation.definitionFit: A British police officer holding the rank next to sergeant in the chain of command.

clue.text: Had enough reason to do this

definitions.text: Had enough reason to do this

parts.words: Had enough reason to do this
parts.note: crying I've had enough is the moment to give up, so having had enough is a reason to yield

explanation.definitionFit: To give in or yield to an opponent is to capitulate, which is what someone who has had enough does.

clue.text: Wants flavour that's insipid

parts.note: taste is the flavour of something
wants here means lacks, as the suffix -less means lacking

explanation.surface: Someone asks for some flavour in food that is bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wants flavour' means lacks flavour, so the lacking suffix comes after the flavour; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland, insipid food has no flavour to speak of, a straight synonym.

clue.text: It's used to hold a cornet in position

indicators.note: to position letters is to set them in a new place, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is used to keep an ice-cream cornet upright in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Any box, tin or vessel is a thing whose purpose is to hold other items.

clue.text: Naturally what you'd expect from a bank teller?

definitions.text: Naturally what you'd expect from a bank teller?

parts.words: Naturally what you'd expect from a bank teller?
parts.note: a teller is both a bank clerk handling customers' money and a storyteller, who naturally gives a narrative

explanation.definitionFit: A bank keeps a customer's money record, and a teller of tales gives a narrative, both senses of this word.

clue.text: Quietly get pig from it and make a pie

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a sty is the pen where a pig is kept, so it is where you go to get one

explanation.surface: A cook goes softly to fetch a pig from somewhere and turns it into a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and make' is a link; A is taken as written from 'a pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish one is a folded pie of pastry filled with meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Shows of force, for instance

parts.note: military marches past are displays of strength by armed forces, one example of public processions

explanation.definitionFit: Military processions are displays staged to show off an army's might.

clue.text: Tempts odd number to take cold refreshment

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of the number are rearranged

parts.note: ten is a number
ices are frozen desserts

explanation.surface: A peculiar figure is persuaded to have a frozen treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges TEN, a number, into ENT; 'to take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or tempt someone is to draw them on with something attractive.

clue.text: Matter sealed in. compact

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the words matter sealed

explanation.surface: Some material is sealed inside a small container.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact speech uses few words, so it is brief and curt.

clue.text: We hear, beat & cane with it

definitions.text: We hear, beat & cane with it

parts.words: We hear, beat & cane with it
parts.note: beat sounds like the root crop beet, and both beet and cane are paired with this sweetener in the names of its two sources

explanation.definitionFit: Sweetener comes from two main crops, beet and cane, and is named after each.

clue.text: Intent on changing a stern bearing

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: changing means the letters of a stern are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to alter the course of a ship's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges A STERN into ARNEST, after E; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being serious and intent on something is a synonym for sincere purpose.

clue.text: Got paid nothing!

parts.note: reads as a complaint about wages, but means obtained something without paying for it, by cadging

explanation.definitionFit: To cadge or beg something without paying is to sponge, the past tense here.

clue.text: Fancy falling asleep?

parts.note: a fancy is a fantasy, and the images that come once you drift off are of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy or fancy, and also the visions experienced during sleep.

clue.text: Concerns businessmen with them

definitions.meaning: go-getting businessmen are said to have drive and initiative, plural here

explanation.definitionFit: A business venture or firm is a concern, and initiative is the quality enterprising people show.
